title: ～に比べて — compared with ～
summary: Sets one thing beside another as a standard of comparison: “compared with ～.” The noun after に is the standard, and the main clause describes the thing being judged. It can be used for people, places, times and so on.

patterns.gloss: noun + に比べて (去年に比べて)
clause + のに比べて (思ったのに比べて)

body.p: In AはBに比べて〜, B is the standard and the degree of A is described against it. The standard comes first, as in 去年に比べて、今年は雨が多い. In writing, に比べ is also used.

It works like より, but に比べて sits easily at the start of a sentence and signals a comparison clearly. 〜と比べると means the same. To use something other than a noun as the standard, add の after the plain form and then に比べて.

examples.ja: 去年（きょねん）に比（くら）べて、今年（ことし）は雨（あめ）が多（おお）い。
examples.romaji: Kyonen ni kurabete, kotoshi wa ame ga ōi.
examples.tr: Compared to last year, there's more rain this year.

examples.ja: 都会（とかい）に比（くら）べて、田舎（いなか）は物価（ぶっか）が安（やす）い。
examples.romaji: Tokai ni kurabete, inaka wa bukka ga yasui.
examples.tr: Compared with the city, the countryside has cheaper prices.

examples.ja: 以前（いぜん）に比（くら）べて、この駅（えき）はずいぶん便利（べんり）になった。
examples.romaji: Izen ni kurabete, kono eki wa zuibun benri ni natta.
examples.tr: Compared with before, this station has become much more convenient.

pitfalls: The standard is the noun before に. Do not mix it up with the thing being judged: AはBに比べて (B is the standard).
The main clause states the result of the comparison. Unlike より, you do not need 〜のほうが.
